claim: The BDE database has 484907 raw rows but only 290664 unique (molecule,fragment1,fragment2) units and 42577 unique molecules, so raw rows are ~1.67x redundant relative to the pair unit, and rows sharing a (molecule,fragment1,fragment2) key never disagree on bde or bond_type.
value_found: 484907 raw rows (gzip line count excluding header = 484907; pandas len = 484907; sha256 2ee36d1548d51289e3faa21e1269b9bbb8f3a8975f9b29719e6beae226864cc6); 290664 unique (molecule,fragment1,fragment2) keys; 42577 unique molecules; redundancy 484907/290664 = 1.668273 (reported 1.6683); 0 keys with >1 distinct bde (max within-key min-max span = 0.0, max within-key SD = 0.0, bde NaN rows = 0); 0 keys with >1 distinct bond_type. Secondary: 290641 unique ordered (fragment1,fragment2) pairs (ratio 1.668405), 290664 unique (mol,f1,f2,bde) 4-tuples and 290664 unique (mol,f1,f2,bond_type) 4-tuples.
unit: raw DB row, collapsed to unique (molecule, fragment1, fragment2) key; cross-checked against unique molecule, unique ordered fragment pair, unique (molecule,bond_index), and unique (mol,f1,f2,bde/bond_type) units.
method: Four independent implementations, none importing output/analysis/common.py: (1) pandas/numpy vectorized groupby-ngroup script /data/user/conversations/conv-75e3fc1d-c4c9-41b5-800b-05f4632eec99/project/output/results/_verify1_fast.py; (2) pure-python csv.DictReader + set/defaultdict streaming script /data/user/conversations/conv-75e3fc1d-c4c9-41b5-800b-05f4632eec99/project/output/results/_verify1_pure.py; (3) shell text path: gzip-decompress to TSV then `cut -f1,2,3 | sort -u | wc -l`, `cut -f1 | sort -u | wc -l`, `cut -f1,2,3,4 | sort -u | wc -l`, `cut -f1,2,3,5 | sort -u | wc -l`; (4) an earlier slow pandas groupby.apply script that also ran to completion with identical counts. All four agree exactly.
notes: All five components reproduce to the reported precision. (a) Row count verified two ways (gzip line iteration and pandas) plus the physical file; sha256 of the .gz recorded. (b) The claimed unit is (molecule,fragment1,fragment2), which is the right one here: it yields 290664, whereas the rate-limiting alternative units differ - unique (fragment1,fragment2) pairs = 290641, unique molecules = 42577, unique (molecule,bond_index) = 484907 (i.e. bond_index makes every row unique). Any ratio other than ~1.67 is a unit error: rows/unique-molecule = 11.3889 and unique-triples/unique-molecule = 6.8268 would be the wrong denominators. (c) The 1.668273 value reconverges to the reported 1.6683 exactly. (d) Consistency is stronger than claimed: not only do 0 keys vary in bde, the max within-key min-max span is exactly 0.0 and max within-key SD is 0.0 (bit-identical floats, not merely equal to rounding), and 0 keys vary in bond_type; there are 0 NaN bde rows and 0 nulls/empty strings in molecule/fragment1/fragment2/bond_type. (e) Mechanism of the inflation: the duplicated keys are symmetry-equivalent bonds of the same molecule (e.g. the 4 C-H bonds of methane appear as 4 raw rows with bond_index 0..3, identical fragment pair and identical bde); 131063 of 290664 keys have multiplicity >1, up to 20 rows per key, and 325306 rows sit in multi-row keys. delta_stereo is constant 0 for all 484907 rows so it contributes zero duplication; no row is duplicated on any subset of the other 7 columns (all-column duplicate rows = 0, all-but-rid duplicate rows = 0). (f) One boundary caveat on the claim's framing, not a contradiction: bde is a deterministic function of (molecule,fragment1,fragment2), but NOT of the fragment pair pooled across molecules - 23 of the 290641 ordered fragment pairs carry 2 distinct bde values (e.g. E- vs Z- or stereoisomeric parents such as C/C=C/C vs C/C=C\C giving 101.491 vs 100.245 for [CH3]+[CH]=CC). So 'rows sharing a key never disagree' holds only at the molecule-resolved key, which is the key the claim names. Also note the DB's fragment-pair count is 290641, not the 539 fragment pairs reported for the benchmark view in claim 12 - different datasets, no conflict.
